reviews.text:
Nebula charged me repeatedly without me realizing I had signed up for anything.

When I first used Nebula, I genuinely believed I was paying just $1 for a one-time astrology reading. Nothing more.

Then, months later, I happened to check my bank statement and noticed multiple charges from Nebula — $29.99 here, $45 there. The shocking part? I had never knowingly signed up for a subscription.

I never saw a clear confirmation that I was enrolling in a paid plan. I didn’t receive an email telling me I had an active subscription. And when I tried to figure out how to cancel it, there wasn’t even an obvious cancellation option.

I reached out to customer support, but received no response.

I searched online and found that many other users were reporting the exact same experience.

Eventually, I had to contact my bank and block further charges because I couldn’t find another way to stop them.

So my question is: How is this allowed?

How can a company charge customers repeatedly without making the subscription terms and consent completely clear? Why should canceling a subscription be so difficult? And how many people are unknowingly losing money every month simply because they don’t check their bank statements?

If you’ve ever used Nebula, I strongly recommend checking your bank account and payment history.

You may be paying for a subscription you never realized you agreed to.
